basic_details.job_title: IIT Kharagpur Junior Research Fellow (Mining Engineering) Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online
basic_details.short_information: The Department of Mining Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, is filling one Junior Research Fellow (JRF) post in a time-bound research project sponsored by Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Limited (CMPDI). The consolidated compensation is up to Rs. 37000 per month, depending on qualification and experience, for 24 months or until the project ends, whichever is earlier. Candidates need an M.Tech, or a B.Tech with a valid GATE score, in the disciplines listed below. Applications are invited online, and the last date is 2 December 2026.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The notice gives the essential qualification in two places. Its summary line asks for a Post Graduate Degree in Basic Science, OR a Graduate / Post Graduate Degree in a Professional Course, selected through a process described in the notice. The detailed section says candidates must hold either of the following: M.Tech in Civil Engineering (Structural or Geotechnical Engineering), Mechanical Engineering (Design or Manufacturing), Mining Engineering, Tunnelling, Applied Mechanics, or any other allied engineering discipline; OR B.Tech in Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mining Engineering, Applied Mechanics, or any allied engineering discipline. A valid GATE score is mandatory for candidates holding a B.Tech degree. B.Tech graduates from Centrally Funded Technical Institutions (CFTIs) with a CGPA greater than 8.0 may be exempted from the GATE score requirement, subject to applicable institute norms. The summary line names two routes of selection for the essential qualification: Scholars selected through National Eligibility Tests: CSIR-UGC NET including lectureship (Assistant Professorship), and GATE. Selection through national-level examinations conducted by Central Government departments and their agencies and institutions such as DST, DBT, DAE, DOS, DRDO, MoE, ICAR, ICMR, IIT, IISc, IISER and NISER. Candidates must have a strong fundamental understanding of Solid Mechanics, particularly stress-strain behaviour, structural deformation and mechanical response under different loading conditions. The notice calls a strong foundation in Solid Mechanics essential. Prior knowledge of Finite Element Analysis (FEA), numerical modelling, experimental stress analysis, strain measurement techniques and programming. Familiarity with ANSYS, ABAQUS, LS-DYNA, MATLAB, Python, strain gauges, Digital Image Correlation (DIC), sensor-based monitoring or AI/ML techniques is an added advantage. Prior experience in AI/ML is desirable but not mandatory, provided the candidate shows an aptitude for computational modelling and interdisciplinary research. The prescribed qualifications and experience are the minimum, and mere possession of them does not entitle a candidate to be called for the interview. Candidates should check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The consolidated compensation is up to Rs. 37000 per month, depending on qualification and experience. The assignment is temporary and lasts 24 months or until the termination of the project, whichever is earlier. The notice mentions no HRA or other allowance.

content_sections.heading: IIT Kharagpur Junior Research Fellow (JRF) Job Description
content_sections.text: The selected candidate will work on AI-enabled Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) of Heavy Earth Moving Machinery (HEMM) operating under varying geo-mining conditions. The research mainly involves experimental investigation and advanced numerical modelling of the structural response, deformation and strain-field evolution of HEMM components under realistic operational loading. The candidate will be involved in: Experimental measurement and analysis of strain and deformation fields in critical structural components of HEMM. Development of advanced numerical models using Finite Element Methods (FEM) to simulate structural behaviour under varying loading and operating conditions. Correlation and validation of experimentally measured strain fields with numerical simulation results. Identification of critical stress concentration zones, deformation patterns and potential structural failure mechanisms. Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques for structural health monitoring, damage detection and predictive maintenance. Development of an integrated experimental-numerical-AI framework for assessing structural integrity and improving the operational reliability of HEMM.
